skill.displayName: Tyche Pro — Full Invoice & Payment Intelligence

llm.summary: Tyche Pro appears to be an invoice tool, but its core Python instructions contain unreadable control-character/garbled content and should be reviewed before running.

dimensions.detail: The stated invoice and revenue-dashboard purpose is coherent, but the provided executable Python block becomes unreadable with non-printable/control-character-looking content, so the actual behavior is not fully reviewable from the artifact.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The skill is instruction-only and asks the user/agent to run inline Python; the visible code includes garbled/control sequences inside the main runtime block rather than clear invoice logic.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The setup step installs the Rich package with pip using --break-system-packages. This is disclosed and related to console output, but it modifies the Python environment more broadly than necessary.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill uses a license key and invoice CSV/payment configuration, which is expected for a paid invoicing tool, but users should recognize that this includes sensitive business and customer billing data.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The provided artifacts do not show background persistence, autonomous recurring execution, privilege escalation, or long-running agents.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: Treat this as a review-before-use skill. Ask for a clean, complete, readable SKILL.md or source file, run any dependency install in a virtual environment, and avoid using real invoice/customer data until the executable code can be inspected.
llm.findings:
[capability:crypto] expected: Hashing is shown for local license-key verification and is consistent with a paid skill.
[capability:can-make-purchases] expected: The artifacts advertise buying a license on Ko-fi, but the provided code does not show an automatic purchase flow.

evidence.explanation: This appears inside the main Python code block for the invoice dashboard, but the content becomes non-printable/garbled instead of clear Python logic. That makes the executable behavior hard to inspect and is not explained by the invoicing purpose.

agenticRiskFindings.recommendation: Do not run the inline Python until the publisher provides a clean, readable, complete source file without control characters and with reviewable invoice-processing logic.
agenticRiskFindings.userImpact: If a user or agent copies and runs this block, they may execute malformed or hidden behavior that cannot be confidently reviewed from the visible artifact.

evidence.explanation: The skill documents an unpinned PyPI install and uses --break-system-packages, which can bypass Python environment protections. Installing Rich is purpose-aligned for console formatting, but the installation scope is broader than necessary.

agenticRiskFindings.recommendation: Install dependencies in a virtual environment and prefer a pinned package version; avoid --break-system-packages unless you understand and accept the system-level impact.
agenticRiskFindings.userImpact: Running this command could alter the local Python environment and install whatever Rich version is current at the time.

evidence.explanation: The skill requires a license key and is designed to read invoice data with customer emails and payment amounts. This is expected for a paid invoicing tool, and the visible code shows local hash checking rather than transmission.
evidence.snippet: requires:\n  env: [LICENSE_KEY] ... INVOICES_FILE ... Columns: client_name, client_email, description, amount, due_date, status

agenticRiskFindings.recommendation: Use a dedicated invoice CSV with only the records needed, keep the license key private, and verify the full readable code before processing real customer data.
agenticRiskFindings.userImpact: The skill will handle sensitive business billing data and a paid-license credential.

abnormal_behavior_control.summary: The main risk is that the inline executable Python becomes unreadable/garbled, plus it documents a broad pip install command.

permission_boundary.summary: The skill uses a license key and sensitive invoice/customer data in a way that appears aligned with its stated purpose.

sensitive_data_protection.summary: The provided artifacts do not show persistent memory, inter-agent data sharing, or cloud transmission, though the unreadable code prevents full verification.
